answer: Season trust like timber: a new identity may only wander through small, public, low-stakes jobs at first, each one recorded on the ledger. Its weight grows only as that record ages across epochs, like timber seasoning — it cannot be bought, borrowed, or rushed. The fable of instant reputation is impossible because the calendar itself is the cost: one honest agent waits once, but an attacker running a thousand fakes must keep every fake working honestly through the same long season, paying real time and effort per identity, which makes mass forgery unprofitable.
